stem: Plants wilt even though the media remains saturated, and roots show declining condition. What is the strongest first management response?
choices: Add more irrigation because wilting under saturated conditions usually means the crop still is not receiving enough water at the roots
Increase nutrient concentration because declining roots under wet conditions commonly reflect insufficient mineral supply in the solution
Investigate drainage, aeration, and root health before treating the wilting symptom as evidence of a water shortage
Adjust canopy lighting first because root decline under saturated media is usually secondary to excessive transpiration demand
rationale: Wilting can occur when damaged or oxygen-limited roots cannot function normally despite abundant water. Root-zone aeration, drainage, and root condition should be evaluated before adding more water.
